basis: Developmental/intellectual impairment >50%; conduction disease and cataracts each >30% over the lifetime. Common GI dysmotility omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental and intellectual impairment affects >50%; congenital muscle weakness defines the dystrophy.
decisions.ocular: involved: characteristic cataracts affect >30% over the lifetime, including survivors of congenital disease.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disease; abnormal muscle fibers 2/2, muscle atrophy 1/2, intellectual disability/seizures 1/2. Hearing-loss frequency is insufficiently established.

decisions.otologic: none: hearing impairment is reported without frequency; a ≥30% rate in syndromic COXPD24 is not established by the supplied evidence.

basis: Glycerol kinase deficiency, adrenal insufficiency and muscular dystrophy define this contiguous-gene syndrome; neurodevelopmental impairment 80-99%; persistent strabismus 30-79%.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent strabismus/esotropia is an ocular alignment disorder with impaired binocular function; HPO frequency 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: muscular dystrophy is a defining component of complex Xp21 deletion syndrome; myopathy occurs in 80-99%.

basis: Autoimmune systemic microvasculopathy without skin fibrosis; esophageal dysfunction ~70-90% and interstitial lung disease ~40-60%.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: structural microvascular injury is intrinsic to systemic sclerosis; this rests on the vasculopathy, beyond transient Raynaud symptoms.

basis: Skeletal and muscle developmental abnormalities define the syndrome; intellectual disability and symblepharon each 30-79%. Numerous nevi do not establish skin dysfunction.

decisions.dermatologic: none: numerous benign nevi occur in 30-79%, but the evidence does not establish destructive, infiltrative or functionally impairing skin disease.

basis: Deep pelvic soft-tissue adipose overgrowth; bladder/ureter compression with obstructive dysfunction occurs in ~30-50%. Constipation alone does not establish bowel damage.

decisions.dermatologic: none: the proliferating fat is in deep pelvic connective tissue, outside the skin and subcutis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: this deep pelvic mesenchymal soft-tissue proliferation is assigned to the connective-tissue axis.

basis: Cavernous venous thrombosis directly impairs adjacent cranial nerves in most patients; residual neuropathy occurs in ~50%. Lasting visual loss is a minority complication.

decisions.neurologic: involved: adjacent cranial nerves suffer direct dysfunction commonly, with residual neuropathy in ~50%; the thrombus originates in a vein.

basis: Predominantly skeletal-muscle dystrophy; cardiac involvement is variable and not securely ≥30% across this umbrella. A cardiomyopathy subtype alone does not establish frequency.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiomyopathy is a recognized subtype, but the evidence does not securely establish cardiac damage in ≥30% across delta-sarcoglycanopathy.

basis: Characteristic caustic oral/GI injury and pulmonary toxicity; direct tubular renal injury occurs in ~40-70%. Functionally significant hepatic injury is not reliably ≥30%.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic injury varies substantially with dose and case severity; ≥30% with functional hepatic damage across the poisoning spectrum is not established.

basis: Abnormal gonadal differentiation with testosterone excess 3/3; cardiac defects, hemidiaphragm aplasia and urogenital sinus malformation each ≥1/3; small cohort limits certainty.

decisions.renal: involved: urogenital sinus malformation affects the urethral outlet, within the renal axis; reported in 1/3 patients.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: aplasia of a hemidiaphragm is a structural skeletal-muscle defect, reported in 1/3 patients.
